alignment.note: Greek marks the genitive analytically with the article + ending (τοῦ εὐαγγελίου); the Peshitta uses the proclitic ܕ- (dalath, genitive/relative particle) on ܐܘܢܓܠܝܘܢ; the Vulgate uses inflection alone (Evangelii). A standard divergence in how each language realises adnominal genitive. [Patched in corpus v1.0.0 — original output mis-classified the Syriac construction as 'construct state'.]

Greek υἱοῦ and Latin Filii are bare nouns; the Peshitta ܒܪܗ carries the 3ms possessive suffix -ܗ (literally 'his son'), with the referent God resolved by the following ܕܐܠܗܐ. A minor expansion of pronominal explicitness characteristic of Syriac. [Patched in corpus v1.0.0 — original output verdict 'aligned' missed the Peshitta possessive suffix.]

Greek marks the genitive with article τοῦ + θεοῦ (articular genitive typical of Koine); the Peshitta marks it with proclitic ܕ- on ܐܠܗܐ (the noun stands in the emphatic state, which itself supplies definiteness in Syriac); the Vulgate uses bare inflection (Dei). Three different grammatical realisations of the same divine title in genitive position. [Patched in corpus v1.0.0 — original output mis-described the Syriac as 'omitting the article' which conflates two distinct grammatical systems.]
